report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned for the online news/blog domain — i.e., to write/structure content in a newspaper/news‑site style (headlines/sections/metadata) and blog/media linkouts, akin to major news sites (e.g., NYT/DailyMail-style content).

Reasoning from evidence:
- Vocabulary shift toward news actors and roles at pos0: top tokens repeatedly include “billionaire,” “politicians,” “activists,” “journalists/journalist,” “spokeswoman/spokesman,” “chairman,” “legislators,” “Obama.” These are classic newswire/newspaper entity/role terms.
- Strong signal for newspaper sections/nav and datelines, especially at pos1 in higher layers (largest norms): tokens like “Political/Politics,” “Sunday,” “literary,” and later “May,” “Mar,” “TV,” “Mail,” “-,” “(” — all typical of section headers and date/metadata lines on news pages.
- Heavy emphasis on blog/media ecosystem in later positions (pos2–pos4) across many high‑norm cells: “blogs,” “blogger,” “blogging,” “Blog,” “photo,” “video,” “film,” “facebook,” “http,” “sexy” (tabloid/entertainment slant), “News,” “USA.” This looks like link/media modules and blogrolls common on news sites.
- “Metropolitan” appears frequently at pos0 and across layers — a canonical newspaper section (e.g., NYT “Metropolitan”), reinforcing a newsroom taxonomy prior.
- Late-layer structure tokens (pos2–pos4) like newline, space, parentheses, colons, list numbers (“\n”, “ ”, “(”, “:”, “No”, “1”, “-”, “...”, “/”, “)”) suggest formatting typical of headlines, bylines, and list/module layouts on news sites.
- Norm concentration: extremely large differences at later layers, especially at position 1, indicate a strong, early, domain-wide prior being injected (front-matter/sectioning before the body), consistent with news/article scaffolding.

Taken together, these point to a finetune that instilled a “news/blog site” behavior: generating or structuring text like online journalism (sections, dates, nav, media/blog linkouts, and newsy entities), rather than generic web text.
